output.summary: A grass native to the Mediterranean region, canary grass is widely grown for birdseed. Its erect, hairless stems carry compact heads resembling club wheat. The seed is eaten in the Canary Islands, Italy and North Africa and prepared as atole in parts of Mexico; its hulls appear to contain silica fibres linked to esophageal cancer, while a hull-less variety was announced for human food.
output.edibilityNote: Seeds are eaten regionally and prepared as atole in parts of Mexico; hulls may contain silica fibres, while a hull-less food variety was announced.
